title: An audit gets a real picture of the app again
goal: The loop photographs the app for every audit the user reads, and right now every one of those pictures is an offscreen drawing of the window rather than the window itself. The app says it is allowed to record the screen and then fails every time it tries, so nobody reading an audit is seeing what the app actually looks like: colours, shadows and anything layered over the window are all missing.
notes:
Reproduced 2026-09-14 23:13 and again at 23:54 and 00:20, three separate probe launches. Scripts/probe-app.sh prints "==> Grants: probe Screen Recording granted" and every snapshot step then logs:

  [0 capture] failed: Error Domain=com.apple.ScreenCaptureKit.SCStreamErrorDomain Code=-3811 "Failed to start stream due to audio/video capture failure"

so <name>.png (the offscreen render) is written and <name>-sc.png never is. Run any walk with a snapshot step to see it, for example Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/path-line-style-walk.json, then look in /tmp/photonz-playtest/path-line-style: four .png files, no -sc.png, and the error above six times in log.json.

It WAS working the day before: Scripts/playtest/out/ in the repo still holds panel-says-less-three-picked-sc.png and panel-says-less-arrange-reference-sc.png written at 2026-09-14 20:27 by the previous task. So something between then and now stopped it, which is the thing to find. Candidates worth checking in order: whether the probe bundle was re-signed with a different identity (the grant is pinned to the code identity, and CLAUDE.md records this exact failure mode for the dev app: "the app shows as granted/on in System Settings but still can not capture"); whether SCShareableContent is being asked for while the probe is not frontmost; and whether the grant check the Grants line prints is asking a different question from the one the capture needs (CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess says undetermined-or-granted, which is not the same as granted).

The fix of last resort is documented in CLAUDE.md and needs a person: tccutil reset ScreenCapture com.dzearing.photonz.probe, relaunch, re-grant. A runner cannot do that, so if that is the answer the task is to make the Grants line SAY so instead of claiming the grant.

Found while auditing a-path-says-what-its-colour-paints-how-thick-its, whose audit had to ship offscreen renders and say so.
acceptance: A walk with a snapshot step writes a real window capture beside its offscreen drawing again
The line the app prints about what it is allowed to do agrees with what it can actually do: if recording is going to fail, it does not claim to be granted
A walk run from a clean start proves it, with the capture file listed in its output

Still broken on 2026-09-15: both audits written overnight say so in their own rough lists (queue/audits/2026-09-15-pane-load.json and queue/audits/2026-09-15-path-line-style.json), so two of the three audits the user has to read this morning have no real picture of the app in them. Raised to p1 and moved to the front by the manager pass: an audit with no photograph is the loop reporting on itself. Probably the same root cause as the walk regression filed the same pass, because the last good -sc.png (2026-09-14 20:27) and the last sweep with the walks green (2026-09-14 16:19) bracket the same evening, and both failures look like the probe window having no real presence on screen.

ANSWER, from a-hundred-and-fifteen-walks-fail-on-code-that-pa: this is the Mac's screen being LOCKED, not the grant. macOS refuses a ScreenCaptureKit stream while the login window is up, which is what -3811 is here.

The timestamps close it. This Mac locked at 2026-09-14 20:46:47 local: CGSSessionScreenLockedTime = 1789444007, and CGSSessionScreenIsLocked has read 1 continuously ever since. The last -sc.png any walk wrote was 20:44 (/tmp/photonz-playtest/appearance-min/b-two-sc.png), two minutes before the lock; every failure written up in the notes above (23:13, 23:54, 00:20) is after it. Nothing was re-signed in between.

So do NOT spend a cycle on tccutil reset or on the code identity. The one check that settles it is one capture with the screen unlocked, and a sweep is already requested that will take it.

Acceptance item two is already done. Scripts/probe-app.sh now reads the lock out of dist/probe-grants.json and its Grants line ends in '· screen locked' or '· screen unlocked', with the cost spelled out underneath, so the app no longer claims it can see something it cannot. Verified tonight:

  ==> Grants: probe Screen Recording granted · this terminal Accessibility denied · screen locked
      THE SCREEN IS LOCKED, so this app is not being drawn at all...

What is left here is acceptance one and three: run any walk with a snapshot step on an unlocked screen and confirm the -sc.png is back.
claimed by go loop

reproduced 2026-09-15 03:10 PDT: the Mac is still locked (CGSSessionScreenIsLocked = 1, locked since 2026-09-14 20:46:47, unbroken). Ran Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/path-line-style-walk.json: exit 3, done.json status "locked", zero steps. So acceptance one and three cannot be executed by any runner today, and the previous pass's diagnosis stands unchallenged.

Found the defect underneath it while looking, and it is the one that let this go unnoticed for two mornings: a refused capture was a log line and NOTHING ELSE. PlaytestHarness.screenCapture caught the error, wrote note(0,"capture","failed: ..."), and the walk carried on green. A run that photographed nothing looked exactly like a run that photographed everything, so an audit written from it shipped the offscreen drawing under the name the capture would have had. Worse, the folder is overwritten rather than emptied, so yesterday's <name>-sc.png sat there waiting to be copied into today's audit.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, before building: the task as written asks a runner to take one photograph, which no runner can do while the Mac is locked, and every pass that claims it will burn a cycle rediscovering the lock. The useful question underneath it is not 'does capture work' but 'how did nobody notice for two mornings', and that has an answer in the code.

WHAT LANDED.

1. A capture that could have been taken and was not now FAILS the walk. PlaytestHarness.screenCapture used to catch the error, write one log line and carry on green, so a run that photographed nothing was indistinguishable from a run that photographed everything. The rule lives in Sources/PhotonzCore/PlaytestCaptureLedger.swift (pure, Sendable, 9 unit tests written first in Tests/PhotonzCoreTests/PlaytestCaptureLedgerTests.swift) and is applied in finish(). It is withheld for the two cases the app did not cause: the screen was locked, or there is no Screen Recording grant.

2. A refusal DELETES any <name>-sc.png an earlier run left. The output folder is overwritten, never emptied, so a stale photograph was sitting under today's name waiting to be copied into an audit.

3. menuShot, panelMenu and rightClick were the worse half and were silently lying. All three set shot = shotURL.lastPathComponent unconditionally, inside the tracking-loop closure, whatever the capture came back with. Reproduced from the run already on disk: /tmp/photonz-playtest/menu-checkmarks/log.json from 2026-09-15 00:43 logs step 4 with state.shot = "capture-menu-history-off-sc.png" while its own note reads 'the open menu is not a window the screen recorder can see', and capture-menu-history-off-sc.png was sitting in that folder dated 2026-09-14 18:41. An audit copying that file by name would have shipped yesterday's picture as today's app. Now the old file is deleted before the menu opens and the step claims a shot only if the file is there afterwards: the same walk re-run logs shot = null for both steps.

4. done.json carries captures (file names) and capturesSaid (one plain sentence), and Scripts/playtest.sh prints it as '==> Window captures: ...'. That is acceptance three's 'capture file listed in its output', and it is what an audit writer reads instead of guessing.

5. queue/bin/runner-prompt.md and docs/design/playtest-harness.md now say all of it, including that 'screen locked' means no picture is possible whatever the grant says. The runner prompt previously told every runner to ship a shot whenever the grant was granted, with nothing about the lock, so tonight's runners would have had to either break that rule or fudge it.

VERIFIED: Scripts/test.sh 6676 tests in 538 suites passed (was 6667). Two walks run end to end against a probe built from this source with PHOTONZ_ALLOW_LOCKED_WALK=1. toolbar-row-narrow: both captures refused, both stale -sc.png deleted (one planted, one real from 2026-09-14 17:36), capturesSaid 'none. The screen was locked, so macOS refuses every one.', status stayed ok because the lock excuses it. menu-checkmarks: three menu shots refused, three stale pictures deleted, shot = null where it used to name a file.

LEFT ROUGH, in this log rather than as a task: a capture that fails for a harmless reason would now turn a green walk red across 322 walks. No retry was built because there is no evidence of that ever happening while the screen was unlocked and the grant held, and untestable retry machinery on a locked screen is worse than none. The sweep requested at the end of this task is the first thing that would show it.

Everything that can be done on a locked screen is done and committed (aa9b1bd0). Acceptance two is met and verified. Acceptance one and three need one photograph of an unlocked window, which no runner can take: the Mac has been locked since 2026-09-14 20:46:47 and was still locked at 03:34 today, checked at the start of this run and again at the end.

Rather than leave a p1 for the next runner to rediscover the lock with, the proof is now automatic. A walk on an unlocked screen with the grant held either writes the -sc.png and names it on its own '==> Window captures:' line, or FAILS naming the step that went unphotographed. So the first walk anyone runs after the screen is unlocked settles this either way, and a sweep is already queued to be that walk.

This task is marked pending, not blocked: blocking with no decision card strands a task for good (queue-lib.mjs setStatus says so out loud), and the only real question here is already on the dashboard as the overnight-lock card against a-hundred-and-fifteen-walks-fail-on-code-that-pa. A second card would be its twin. Instead this task now DEPENDS on that one, so it is not claimable until the lock question is settled and a walk can run, and then it is a ten second check.

To close it by hand: unlock the screen, run Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/toolbar-row-narrow-walk.json, and read the Window captures line.

EVIDENCE THAT THE LOCK VERDICT IS TOO BROAD, from 2026-09-15 17:3x. The Mac still reads locked (ioreg -n Root -d1 -a | grep -A1 CGSSessionScreenIsLocked returns <true/>, and every launch prints 'screen locked'), and a screen capture taken under that very verdict came back as a FULLY DRAWN window: queue/audits/2026-09-15-layer-pick-many-rows.png, 2560x1680, the real editor with its traffic lights, its shadow, the dock, five layer rows and the picked row highlighted, sitting over the dashboard behind it.

So on this machine, in this lock state: compositing works, screen capture works, and the accessibility names work (selectRow picked rows by name all through an 84 step walk). What does NOT work is tutorial anchors: tutorial-layers-and-undo-walk fails at step 23 waiting on tutorialStep(put-it-back), and it fails identically on unmodified main.

That matters because the gate is currently all-or-nothing, and three audits in a row have shipped with no picture on a premise that is only partly true here. Worth considering: let a walk RUN when the lock reads true but a test capture of the app's own window comes back non-blank, and keep the refusal for whatever actually is broken (anchors), rather than refusing everything. Reproduce with: PHOTONZ_ALLOW_LOCKED_WALK=1 Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/layer-pick-at-scale-walk.json, then look at many-sc.png in the output folder.
